climate_admin.intro: LocalHome is run from here without touching any file or code: the season, the apartment's Shelly devices, the operating settings, maintenance and the board's status.

Stop the process yourself (Ctrl+C in its terminal) and start it again, then reload this page - fine for developing on Windows, this is a non-issue on the Linux box you'd actually deploy to.

climate_admin.valve_test_hint: Manual test - the thermostat takes back control on its next cycle.
climate_admin.manual_no_value: No manual value set yet - enter one below.
climate_admin.extra_switches_note: Two more fixed, standalone Shelly Plus 1 on/off switches, not tied to a zone and with no sensor - leave either blank if not wired yet. If config.yaml's thermostat.interlocks/mode_switches already control one of these by a different name, update that config.yaml entry to say "Bathroom Bypass Valve"/"Dehumidifier" instead - this panel always uses those exact names.
climate_admin.extra_sensor_note: A fixed Shelly H&T Gen3 sensor, not part of any zone: the outdoor temperature and humidity, in the chip at the top and the climate chart. Until the sensor is installed leave it Simulated: the temperature and the chart still show, marked as simulated. With None it doesn't appear.
climate_admin.how_it_works_heading: How it works - everything in brief
climate_admin.how_it_works_threshold: A Shelly H&T Gen3 sensor sleeps almost all the time, to make its battery last, and wakes up to send a reading in two cases: at once, when the temperature or humidity has moved at least as much as the thresholds set in the Shelly app (say 0.5 °C and 1%) since its last report; and every 2 hours regardless, even if nothing changed. Every report carries the exact value of that moment, to a tenth of a degree: the thresholds only decide when the sensor speaks up in between, not how precise it is. That's why at night, with the house still, the chart steps down by 0.1 °C every 2 hours or so, and "updated 1h ago" is normal up to 2 hours. Tighter thresholds mean more reports and a battery that lasts less, above all on weak Wi-Fi, where every wake-up costs more. After the board restarts a zone has no reading until the sensor's next report, 2 hours at most; pressing the sensor's button makes it report at once. Only a reading older than 4 hours - two reports missed in a row - counts as not reachable. Two details measured on these sensors: a change report doesn't move the regular one, which stays every 2 hours on its own clock; and the thresholds count from the last value sent. In a steady house nearly all the extra reports are for humidity: the temperature seldom moves half a degree. In Shelly device health each sensor shows its regular and change reports of the last 24 hours, and when the next regular one is due.
climate_admin.how_it_works_wifi: A zone card's WiFi signal figure (shown next to its reading, when reported) below "fair" means the sensor is spending more of its battery retrying its connection, not just reporting slower - moving it closer to the broker's access point, or adding a repeater, fixes battery drain that a firmware update or a config change here cannot.
climate_admin.how_it_works_battery: Battery percentage is shown inline with each zone's reading, highlighted once it's at or below 10% - the same threshold the main dashboard's own low-battery popup uses. Replacing the batteries clears it on the sensor's next report; there's nothing to reset here.
climate_admin.how_it_works_failsafe: If a zone's sensor stays unreachable (not just quiet - actually unreachable, see above) for longer than its failsafe threshold (24h by default), its valve is forced closed automatically rather than left frozen in whatever it was doing indefinitely - shown on that zone's card below as it approaches and crosses the threshold. It clears itself the moment the sensor reports again. To open that valve anyway before the sensor comes back (e.g. while replacing its battery), use Diagnostic mode below.
climate_admin.how_it_works_diagnostic: Diagnostic mode (below) is the way to move any valve by hand regardless of what any sensor says - for verifying a relay actually switches, figuring out which physical valve is which name, or riding out a sensor failsafe or an extended away period without waiting.
climate_admin.diagnostic_note: Takes over every valve and extra switch: the thermostat and the safety rules stop, and each valve moves only from the buttons below. Turning it off hands control back at once, no restart needed.
climate_admin.diagnostic_active_banner: Diagnostic mode is ON - the thermostat and all interlocks are hands-off. Every valve below only moves when you press its button.
climate_admin.diagnostic_confirm_on: Turn on diagnostic mode? The thermostat and all interlocks will stop controlling every valve until you turn this back off.
climate_admin.failsafe_active: Failsafe active: this sensor has been unreachable for {hours}h, past its threshold - its valve has been forced closed automatically. It will resume normal control the moment the sensor reports again, or use Diagnostic mode above to open it sooner.
climate_admin.failsafe_pending: Sensor unreachable for {hours}h - its valve stays as it was for now; it'll be forced closed automatically at {threshold}h unless the sensor recovers first.
climate_admin.system_note: The state of the installation itself rather than of one zone: what didn't load and why, which devices aren't responding, whether the control and recording loops are running, and the process, disk and history numbers that tell a slow problem (memory growing, disk filling up) apart from normal. Refreshed every 15 seconds.

climate_admin.settings_note: The operating parameters, changed here without touching any file or code. An empty field uses config.yaml's value (or the default). They take effect after LocalHome restarts, except where the field says otherwise.
climate_admin.settings_defaults_confirm: Remove every setting made here and go back to config.yaml's?
climate_admin.setting_hysteresis_c_help: How far the temperature must move from the target before a valve opens or closes. 0.5 is the Shelly H&T's reporting step: smaller means more short openings.
climate_admin.setting_thermostat_poll_seconds_help: How often the thermostat re-checks the zones. 60 is plenty for a radiant system.
climate_admin.setting_sensor_failsafe_hours_help: If a sensor sends no reading for this long, its zone's valve is closed.
climate_admin.setting_history_retention_days_help: Older data is deleted every day.
climate_admin.setting_history_max_db_mb_help: Hard ceiling on the history database: over it, the oldest days are deleted.
climate_admin.guide_step1: Pick heating or cooling: it applies to the whole plant, and each has its own schedule (painted from the dashboard).
climate_admin.guide_step2: Enter each Shelly's id - every zone's sensor and valve, the bypass, the dehumidifier, the outdoor sensor, the VMC - and save. The id is shown in the Shelly app.
climate_admin.guide_step3: Devices and settings apply after 'Restart LocalHome': the button appears after every save.
climate_admin.guide_step4: Every card says whether its device answers; the overview at the top sums it all up and System status has the details.
climate_admin.how_seasons: Each zone has a target for every hour of the week, from the active season's schedule. Heating opens a valve when the room drops below target minus the hysteresis and closes it above target plus the hysteresis; cooling does the opposite. An hour with no schedule (✕) keeps the valve closed. 'Away' closes everything until the chosen date. The thermostat re-checks the zones continuously (the pace is set in Settings) and compares each valve's real state every time: one opened or closed by hand is corrected.
climate_admin.how_bathrooms: While cooling, the Bathrooms zone is excluded to avoid condensation: its valve stays closed and is re-checked every cycle. The bathroom bypass valve switches on for cooling and off for heating by itself. The dehumidifier is switched by hand, but only while cooling: switching to heating turns it off and hides it.
climate_admin.how_vmc: Ventilation runs continuously: the dashboard picks its speed - Night 20%, Day 50%, Boost 100% - or any value with the slider. Picking a mode starts it again if it was stopped from the Shelly app.
climate_admin.how_missing: A device that's off, not installed or unreachable never stops the rest: its card says so, System status lists it as a problem, it writes nothing to the history, and the log notes it once (then one line every 10 minutes). A device that has to be asked actively (the VMC) is asked less and less often until it answers.
climate_admin.how_data: The charts' history has a day limit and a size limit (in Settings): past them, the oldest data is deleted. System logs live in RAM (30 MB at most), don't wear the eMMC and are lost at reboot. Before any deletion in Maintenance a backup is saved on the board (the last 10, plus one history copy if there's room).
climate_admin.vmc_pick_device: Choose which device the program controls.
climate_admin.vmc_program_moved: The VMC's day/night program is set on the dashboard, on the VMC's own card next to its speed buttons.

climate_admin.led_note: The board's LED matrix shows LocalHome's state to whoever is standing in front of the box, without a phone - above all when the network or LocalHome itself isn't working, which is exactly when this page won't open. On every screen the top-right pixel blinks: LocalHome is alive and drawing.
climate_admin.led_status_running: Connected: the matrix shows the state live.
climate_admin.led_status_no_router: This board has no link to a microcontroller (it isn't an Arduino UNO Q, or the arduino-router service is stopped): the matrix stays dark. The mirror below still shows what it would draw.
climate_admin.led_status_no_sketch: LocalHome's sketch isn't loaded on the microcontroller, so the matrix isn't showing the state. It's loaded once, from the board, with arduino-cli - after installing the Arduino_RouterBridge library if it isn't there yet: every command is in step 11 of the quick installation guide (docs/quick-installation-arduino-uno-q.md). No LocalHome restart needed.

climate_admin.led_now_boot: Start-up: the board's IP address, {ip}, scrolling by.

climate_admin.led_legend_cool: Snowflake: cooling season. Zone bars as above.
climate_admin.led_legend_away: House: away mode on, valves closed until you're back.
climate_admin.led_legend_diagnostic: Wrench: the thermostat isn't driving the valves; they're switched by hand from this panel.
climate_admin.led_legend_idle: Dash: no zone has been configured yet.
climate_admin.led_legend_problem: A blinking exclamation mark and a two-character code (see the table below). With more than one problem they take turns, with the normal screen in between.

climate_admin.led_legend_silence: Blinking X: the microcontroller hasn't heard anything for 20 seconds. LocalHome has stopped, hung or is restarting - if it lasts more than a minute, restart the board.
climate_admin.led_legend_waiting: A dot running along the bottom: the board is on but LocalHome hasn't started yet (the first seconds after power-up).

climate_admin.zones_note_more: Switching from "Shelly" to another source only stops talking to that device: nothing is ever sent to it. A simulated valve can still be tested, with the card's open/close buttons too, before a real relay is wired. A card saying "saved, but not running yet" needs a restart before its status tells you anything useful.
climate_admin.diagnostic_note_more: It covers both zones' valves and the extra switches that are wired (bathroom bypass, dehumidifier). While it's on no interlock or season switch touches them, not even to force a safe state: every valve stays where you left it, or where its last command before it was turned on left it.

climate_admin.watchdog_none: Nothing so far: it hasn't been needed.
climate_admin.wd_radio_on: The Wi-Fi radio was off: switched back on
climate_admin.wd_profile_fixed: Wi-Fi network "{all}": reconnects for ever, power saving off
climate_admin.wd_reconnect: No network for {a} min: reconnecting the Wi-Fi

climate_admin.wd_reboot: No network for {a} min: rebooting the board

climate_admin.wd_killed: LocalHome hung for 2 minutes: restarted by the watchdog
climate_admin.wd_boot_reconnect: Wi-Fi reconnected once after start-up (normal, a precaution)
climate_admin.system_problem_lan_unreachable: The Shelly devices haven't reached the board for {subject}, although the board is on and connected to the Wi-Fi: almost certainly the router. Restart the router.
climate_admin.led_code_RT: the devices can't reach the board although it's on the Wi-Fi: restart the router
climate_admin.how_network: The board stays on the Wi-Fi day and night: power saving is off, it never stops trying to connect, and a watchdog checks every minute that the router answers - when it doesn't, it reconnects the Wi-Fi (3 minutes), restarts the network manager (10), tries again (20) and finally reboots the board (30, at most every 6 hours). All it does goes in the Watchdog history, under System status. The page and the Shellys use the board's name (name.local), not its address: when the router hands out new addresses nothing changes.
climate_admin.how_network_router: One thing the board can't see by itself: the router answering it but no longer passing it the other devices' connections. It happened on the home board: pings got through, the page and the sensors didn't, until the router was restarted. When the Shellys all stop arriving at once while the Wi-Fi is connected, LocalHome says so here in System status and with RT on the LED matrix, and the watchdog reconnects the Wi-Fi; if that's not enough, restart the router. To prevent it: in the router, 5 GHz on a fixed channel between 36 and 48 (channels 52-144 are "radar" ones the router may leave by itself), the board and the Shellys on the main network, never the guest one, and a fixed address for the board if possible. If the page won't open but the LED matrix draws normally, the board is fine: it's the network.
climate_admin.wd_lan_silent: No Shelly connected for {a} min although the router answers: Wi-Fi reconnected (if that's not enough, restart the router)
climate_admin.wd_lan_back: The Shellys reach the board again
climate_admin.shelly_note: What each Shelly says about itself: Wi-Fi signal, internal temperature, restarts, firmware updates and, for battery sensors, whether their reports arrive on time. Battery sensors sleep: they're read when they wake (at least every 2 hours, or when temperature and humidity change). Mains-powered ones are asked every 5 minutes. Read only: nothing is changed on the devices. Signal: above -65 dBm excellent, down to -75 good, down to -85 weak but usable, below that critical.

climate_admin.system_problem_device_reports_missed: {subject}: reports lost over the last 24 hours (weak signal or battery)
